solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rescue brute, grabbing end of tail

indicators.note: grabbing means the first piece takes hold of the second inside it

parts.note: a brute is a savage

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word tail

explanation.surface: Someone saves a beast by seizing hold of its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts L, the last letter of 'tail' picked by 'end of', inside SAVAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to rescue it from loss or wreckage, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bound to get on diving platform

parts.note: to bound is to spring or leap
to board is to get on a vehicle

explanation.surface: Something is sure to end up on the diving platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but 'Bound' is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A springboard is the flexible board divers jump from, a kind of diving platform.

parts.note: legs are limbs, members of the body
to nail something is to pin it

explanation.surface: A way of handing something over that involves body parts and a nail.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; leg spin is a style of slow bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg spin is a kind of bowling in cricket, so a variety of ball delivered.

indicators.note: fake suggests the letters of my hat set's are forged into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise that a set of jewels is counterfeit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my hat!' looks like an exclamation of surprise; all nine letters with the S of 'Set's' are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethysts are violet quartz crystals used as precious stones in jewellery.

clue.text: English bishop with task to perform

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
and means together with

explanation.surface: An English bishop has a job to do.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled Right Reverend, abbreviated RR.
explanation.definitionFit: An errand is a short trip or job one is sent to do, a small chore.

clue.text: Band's mega hit Motown initially put out

indicators.note: put out means a letter is ejected from the word before it

parts.note: a huge hit record is a smash

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word Motown

explanation.surface: A pop group's biggest record, released by the Motown label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' removes M, the first letter of 'Motown' picked by 'initially', from SMASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip or band of cloth worn over the shoulder or round the waist.

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A son staying in causes upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives offence' reads as 'upsets someone', but 'offence' is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a wrongdoing or transgression against moral law.

parts.note: FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loudly

explanation.surface: Jeering at a tiny firm in a raised voice.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff is to jeer or ridicule, the same as to mock.

indicators.note: not tells us to drop the following letter from the word before

parts.note: a brogue is a strong regional accent, especially Irish

explanation.surface: A baddie's way of speaking is plainly foreign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes B from BROGUE. The 's is read as 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, so a villain in the ordinary sense.

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a private soldier, one from the ranks, is a ranker

explanation.surface: A grudge held by a lowly soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' says RANKER is heard, giving a word that sounds the same in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-lasting resentment or ill will.

definitions.meaning: a place booked in advance, as at a restaurant
a qualification or condition attached to agreement

explanation.definitionFit: Reservation covers both a table held for a diner and a proviso or doubt limiting acceptance.

clue.text: Down the back of one's neck, mostly

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its final letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: the nape is the back of the neck

explanation.surface: Soft hairs growing on the back of the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the final E from NAPE. 'Down' is not a direction but soft fluff.
explanation.definitionFit: Nap is the soft raised pile on cloth, a fuzzy surface like down.

indicators.note: holding means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farm hands
to cuff is to strike with the hand

explanation.surface: Workers on strike are being held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the containment signal. 'strike' suggests industrial action by the labourers, but here it is a blow with the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Handcuffs are metal rings locking the wrists, so as a verb it means restrains a prisoner.

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad or appalling
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A dreadful French record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appalling' looks like an anagram signal but gives CHRONIC, informal British for dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a written historical account of events, a record in time order.

clue.text: To expel almost all of gang is hard

indicators.note: almost all of says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a band is a gang of people
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Throwing out nearly a whole gang is tough work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all of' trims the D from BAND, leaving BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish is to send someone away or drive them out, a synonym of to expel.

clue.text: Quite right for salesperson to come back

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: to come back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: It is only fitting for the salesman to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is not a link word here but supplies letters meaning 'in favour of'; 'to come back' is the reversal signal on the salesperson.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper means correct or fitting, as in the proper way to behave.

clue.text: Ancient document with syrup spread across a page

indicators.note: across means the shuffled letters stretch around the other pieces
spread suggests the letters of syrup are smeared into a new order

explanation.surface: An old manuscript has syrup smeared over one of its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges SYRUP as PYRUS, and 'across' puts it around A + P.
explanation.definitionFit: Papyrus is the writing material of ancient Egypt, and a manuscript written on it.

indicators.note: Endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to discuss something is to talk about it

explanation.surface: Talk about an athletics event goes on without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the last S from DISCUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus is an athletics field event in which a heavy disc is thrown.

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
a mission is a vocation or calling

explanation.surface: A daughter is following her vocation in order to win acknowledgement.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is an acknowledgement that something is true, a sense of recognition.

parts.note: mean means low or base in character

explanation.surface: Someone was thinking of a cold spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Meant is the past of mean, to intend, so had in mind.

indicators.note: Extremely here means the extremes, the first and last letters, of palatable

explanation.surface: A very tasty vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' takes the outer letters of 'palatable', P and E, not an intensifier.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea is a small round green seed eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Not all stand by doctor, a radical

indicators.note: Not all says the word is shortened by a letter at the end

parts.note: to stick by someone is to stand by them

explanation.surface: Not everyone supports the radical doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all' trims the K from STICK; the pieces go DR + A + STIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic measures are extreme and far-reaching, close in meaning to radical.

indicators.note: sent over in a down clue means the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A miner's bonus is passed on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a small sum given for service, a gratuity.

clue.text: Dog belonging to Alec, or Giles

indicators.note: belonging to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pet owned by one of two men, Alec or Giles.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Alec' through 'or' into 'Giles'.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II.

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

explanation.surface: Ending up runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop is to come to an end or bring something to a finish.

indicators.note: Complicated suggests the letters of tests on are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Elaborate trials carried out on a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat, named after its American maker.
